questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to find a student friendly destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received an e-mail one week before the beginning of the semester

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to one introduction meeting at my host university. Charles University offered a "buddy-programme" to all exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Follow the erasmus in prague group on instagram. I found housing through one of their coordinators. It is and very easy and safe way to find a shared student appartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a bit more expensive but in my opinion it is worth it. The dormitories are located very long from the city center and they are old and dirty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was completely different compared with how the registration process works at Copenhagen University. In the first week of the semester, you had the opportunity to attend all the courses. It was really nice that you had the opportunity get an impression of the level of the course, the teacher etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a "first come, first served" process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received an e-mail with all important information about the registration process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got 80% of the courses that I wanted to attend even though I carefully followed the registration process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process was a bit of a mess because many of the courses had limited capacity. In spite of the fact that I was ready to sign up from the minute where the registration process opened, I did not manage to get all the courses I wanted to attend. Though, it is important to know that some teachers will allow you to attend to the courses even though the course is fully booked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme is lower compared with KU. But it was nice to have a semester that was a bit more relaxed compared to my home university

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied a lot from course to course. In some courses, the academic level was low which meant that you did not apply the juridical method at all. It was rather about memorizing information than applying the juridical method. Some other courses had a higher academic level, but still not as a high as KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses were not that interactive and the teaching style was in general more old school which meant that you mostly had to listen to presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law, Intellectual Property Law, International Double Taxation Law, Sports and Medical Law, Introduction to Public International Law in the Czech Legal Context, Introduction into Central European Legal Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law. I really liked the course and the teacher is fantastic. The classes were very interactive with a lot of intersting discussions.

questions.answer: I had to buy a subscription at Vodafone to get unlimited wifi

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many things are cheaper than in Denmark. But beer was extremely cheap. It was also cheap to go to cafe's and restaurants

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many different associations

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Charles University have many associations that you can sign up to. They also arranged a ball in the autumn.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the intensive czech language course even though you may not get the credits. I attended the language course and met many Erasmus students from different countries. I did not really know any other students before I went on exchange. It was a great way to find new friends before the beginning of the semester since I met a lot of other exchange students who were in the exactly same situation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Plzen and Brno

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that hard to adjust to the local culture. Czech people are in general very laid back.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really socialize with local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Czech people can sometimes be a bit rude

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cozy atmosphere in Prague

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Sign up for the Intensive Czech Language Course 
2. Follow Erasmus in Prague on instagram and join the Whats App group
3. Find housing on your own

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow erasmus in prague on instagram. It is an easy and safe way to find housing on your own. They have some coordinators who can help you finding a student-friendly shared apartment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was to get out of my comfort zone and improving my academic english skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Socializing with new people

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
